title: Remix is the silliest new Google Photos feature, but I can't stop using it
key_facts: Android Police says Google Photos silently added 15 new Remix templates and widened the rollout of several Create tab features to more regions.
Remix lets a user pick a photo, choose a style and get an AI-transformed version in seconds; it is powered by Google's Imagen model.
The original set had four styles: 3D animation, anime, sketch and comic book.
The writer liked three new templates, called washing machine, fish eye and microwave, which warp a photo in bizarre ways; he found the red carpet one cringe.
Birthday cards and photo-booth style shots are two more of the 15, per Google's rollout notes.
The writer says none of the results could pass as real photos and Remix also changes facial expressions and features.
The new templates are limited to users 18 and older and only available in select countries; Remix also works on iPhone.
quote_evidence: Google Photos silently added 15 new Remix templates, along with a wider rollout of several other Create tab features across more regions.
The new templates are limited to users 18 and older, and only available in select countries.
None of these results could pass as an authentic photo anywhere, and I mean that literally, not as a minor caveat.
why_it_matters_hint: Playful AI photo tools are reaching ordinary phones, though with age and country limits and clearly artificial results.
notes: Hands-on opinion piece by one writer; no Google statement was read directly. Rollout date is not stated, so treated as new.
